messages.subject: engine crash in MCDS analysis
messages.body_plain:
Dear List,

I'm working with 14 frugivore species in Luzon island,
Philippines--comparing species densities, encounter rates, effective
strip widths, and detection functions across three different path
types. While running an MCDS analysis using a combination of
covariates with variance estimation, the distance engine suddenly
crashed and gave me two error messages reproduced below. I can no
longer open the original file I was working on as the same error
message appears every time. It did suggest I contact the programme
developers in case it's a bug. I'd be very grateful if anyone here can
shed some light into this. I can email a copy of my data file if
needed.

* ERROR message No.1:

  Run-time error '-2147213703(80041e79)':

  Fatal error occured in NEngine server. Error message returned from
server: 'Unexpected error in Distance Database Engine.
  Source: D6NEH.NEngineHost.StopItemRunNow
  Internal Error number: -2147418105.
  Internal error description: "Automation error
  The callee (server [not server application] is not available and
disappeared; all connections are invalid. The call may have
executed.".'

* ERROR message No.2:

  The following internal error has occured in Distance:

  Unexpected error in Distance Database Engine.
  Source: D6DbEng.ProjectDatabase.OpenJetDatabase
  Internal Error number: 3343
  Internal Error description: "Unrecognized database format
'C:\Documents and Settings\egs\My Documents\My Distance
Projects\2ndYr_HabData.dst'.".

  (Error raised from: Distance.ClsProject.OpenProjectDatabase)
  (Error source: D6DbEng.ProjectDatabase.OpenJetDatabase)
  (Error number: -2147211505)

Much obliged,

Carmela P. Espa=F1ola
carmela....@gmail.com

--

messages.subject: Questions about point transect intervals
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am a master's student in Brazil and I am trying to analyze data from a
five year point transect sampling. The data was collected

in 216 points, that were located every 200 meters (6 plots of 36 points in
3 different regions, 2 plots in each region).

I have some questions about the software and I wonder if you could help me
by answering whatever is possible from the list below.

Here are the questions:

1 - There were 14 visits in 5 years (the same survey effort for every

point, 3 or 4 visits in a year);

I believe I have to put the number 14 in the sampling fraction, which will

divide (/) the density estimated for 14, right?

And do I have to put the number 14 even if the specie was not registered in
every visits?

2 - Because I need to use the multiplier above, I can=92t stratify the data

in region or year in CDS engine analysis, can I?

So, it is only possible to do global analysis with multipliers in Distance
6.0.

3 - The data is grouped in only 4 intervals and I don=92t have exact
distances (cutpoints: 0-10m, 10-25m, 25-50m and 50-100m).

I've read that the ideal is to have at least 5 or 6 intervals. I'd like to

know if it is possible to have good estimates analyzing these

data with 4 intervals.

4 - I'm reading the user=92s guide, but I still don't understand if I don=
=92t

put a column with the size of the area, it will affect the density
estimated? Considering that the area is the same for each point, and the

same in each plot (1 km=B2).

5 - I don't understand also, if I have to put only the points where the

bird was registered, or if I have to put the points where I have absence
too.

I'm not sure if, when I put only the points where I have records and not

the 216 points sampled in each visit, the program will "understand"

that the animal was there in every visit.

Here is an example of how I am importing the data (in .txt):

year         point                distance

2005       AV-MA-5-1      75

2005       AV-MA-6-4      37.5

2006       AV-MA-4-4      75

2008       AV-MA-2-3      75

...

*OR*

Ducke        AV-MA-1-8       5

=85

* In this case AV-MA-6-2 is the plot 6 and the point 2 in this plot. Is

there any problem to put the point this way?

Thank you very much for your time and attention and I look forward to
hearing from you.

Regards,

--=20

Nayara Tartari Soto
Bi=F3loga
Programa de P=F3s-Gradua=E7=E3o em Ecologia

messages.subject: Errors with Hazard Rate, data structure and stratification
messages.subject_clean: Errors with Hazard Rate, data structure and stratification
messages.body_plain:
Dear List,

I have two questions, one on how to solve an error message from Program
Distance and another regarding data structure and stratification.  Our data
are from point counts along transects in two large river systems (regions)
in Montana. Counts were conducted in 3 years each separated by 4 years
(although not all sites were sampled in all years). Our primary goal is to
examine changes in density across time.

The most glaring issue I'm dealing with is error messages when fitting MCDS
models with a hazard rate key function. Models with Half-normal key
functions produces reasonable estimates at the global, regional, and
transect levels - although 1 or 2 of the more complex half-normal models
produce the same error. The error messages I receive are:

** Error: Analysis engine terminated unexpectedly (with error code
-1073741663).  **....

** Warning: There are no cluster size observations selected.
Cannot estimate expected cluster size. **
 ** Internal Error 53: Mismatched modules -            2
0           0
           0  **
 ** Internal Error 54: Mismatched stats -            4
0           0
           0           2  **

-- End of Analyis Engine Log File --
** Warning: Analysis engine wrote some output to the console error stream,
reproduced below. **
-- Start of Console Error Stream --
forrtl: severe (161): Program Exception - array bounds exceeded

Image              PC        Routine            Line
Source
MCDS.exe           00438F74  GETPARMS                  200  Dmod.for

-- End of Console Error Stream --

 What is causing these errors and how do I change my model specification or
data input to fix them?

Secondly, I am struggling with how to structure the analysis to best
estimate density in each time period at the transect level, while still
incorporating potential heterogeneity in detection probability among
regions and time. Detection probability may vary between regions and among
time periods likely due to differences or changes in vegetation
structure.  Would
it be best to use the region as the region level within the analysis and
post-stratify by year (included as a variable in the point transect data
level)? Or use year as the region data level and use the geographic region
as a covariate for the detection function? In other words, which should
receive greater weight in the structure of the data: space or time? Would
it be appropriate to use MCDS to guide the stratification structure of the
data?

Thanks for any assistance you may be able to offer! Please respond to
joshua....@umontana.edu with any suggestions.

--
Joshua Goldberg
Research Associate
joshua....@umontana.edu
Natural Sciences 305
The University of Montana
Missoula, MT 59812

--

messages.subject: Multiple comparisons
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would like to compare 3 density estimates by different methods for
several bird species. The methods are line transect, point transect and
area search.

There are some large differences in estimates which I interpret as
failure of the method assumptions (e.g. movements for point counts). I
would like show that some of these differences are significant.

Looking at the results:
	Variances are not always equal.
	Some CVs exceed 20%.
	Sample sizes (degrees of freedom) vary and are sometimes small (< 30).

Statistical comparisons I could apply are:
	Multiple Z-tests (3 tests per species).
	Multiple t-tests (optional unequal variance t-test).
	ANOVA.

Applying multiple two-sample tests increase the probability of a Type I
error. I might adjust the critical probability with a Bonferroni
correction: 0.05/3 = 0.017, at the risk of increasing Type II error
rates.

The Z test is very simple but poor if sample sizes are small. I do not
know how to compute degrees of freedom for t-tests with the DISTANCE
results, perhaps Sattherwaite method (Buckland et al. 1993, p. 89):

df = (sum (CVi^2))^2 / sum ((CVi^4) / dfi)

ANOVA may not be reliable with unequal variances, unbalanced sample
sizes and high CVs. I do not know how to compute ANOVA from the DISTANCE
results: which sample sizes to use (ni) and degrees of freedom.

I have searched the DISTANCE mailing list archives and can't find all
the answers to my questions. I do not have access to either of the
modern distance sampling texts (introduction and advanced). I might have
to purchase one, does one of these books detail ANOVA procedures?

This study is exploratory and I do not require definitive results. At
present, I have used multiple Z-tests.

Stephen.

--

messages.subject_clean: Errors with Hazard Rate, data structure and stratification
messages.body_plain:
Joshua:

There are some hints in the error message to indicate what might be
taking place.  Specifically, the message reports a challenge with
cluster size.  Using my powers of extra-sensory perception, I'm guessing
you have cluster size as a covariate in your detection function, true?
So Distance has produced a warning that (perhaps because of
bootstrapping?) there may be instances where a detection function is
requested for which all cluster sizes are the same?  Is that a
possibility in your data?

The fatal errors regarding exceeding an array bound is less easy to
diagnose.  My suspicion is that you may have specified an overly
enthusiastic detection function model (how many covariates are you
trying to incorporate?).  If I were trying to debug this error, I would
simplify the detection function I am trying to fit, and see if that
stops the error message.

Finally on the matter of stratification.  I think you are struggling
with the capability of specifying only a single level of
stratification.  A simple fix for that is to manufacture as many strata
as you have unique combinations of region and year.  You have 2 regions
and 3 years of data; then simply create 6 strata.  It might not be
elegant, but it is functional.
